9fa0d141-d019-4ad7-8bc5-42196ee308bd.2: Prometheus instances, their reported software version, and elapsed seconds since each process started. Uptime resets when the process restarts.
9fa0d141-d019-4ad7-8bc5-42196ee308bd.4: Time spent synchronizing discovered scrape targets, summed per second over five minutes and converted to milliseconds of synchronization work per second. This is workload, not the average duration of one synchronization.
9fa0d141-d019-4ad7-8bc5-42196ee308bd.5: Current number of targets discovered by Prometheus service discovery, summed per Prometheus instance. Discovered targets are not necessarily healthy or successfully scraped.
9fa0d141-d019-4ad7-8bc5-42196ee308bd.7: Average observed interval between scrapes over five minutes, in milliseconds. Compare with the configured scrape interval; this is spacing between scrapes, not the duration of fetching one target.
9fa0d141-d019-4ad7-8bc5-42196ee308bd.8: Scrape failures or rejected samples per second over one minute, grouped by Prometheus instance and failure reason. Reasons include body/sample limits, duplicate timestamps and out-of-order or out-of-bounds samples. These are selected ingestion failures, not all possible target connectivity failures.
9fa0d141-d019-4ad7-8bc5-42196ee308bd.9: Samples appended to the in-memory time-series database per second, averaged over five minutes. Higher rates increase ingestion and storage work.
9fa0d141-d019-4ad7-8bc5-42196ee308bd.11: Current number of time series in the Prometheus in-memory head. Growth can indicate more targets or more label combinations and usually increases memory demand.
9fa0d141-d019-4ad7-8bc5-42196ee308bd.12: Current number of chunks in the Prometheus in-memory head. Chunks hold recent samples; this is a count, not their memory size.
9fa0d141-d019-4ad7-8bc5-42196ee308bd.14: Prometheus query evaluations per second over five minutes, counted at the inner evaluation stage. Use this to see changes in query workload from dashboards, rules and API clients.
9fa0d141-d019-4ad7-8bc5-42196ee308bd.15: Reported 90th-percentile duration of each query execution stage, in milliseconds, taking the largest value across selected instances. The percentile comes from Prometheus internal summaries and is not recalculated over the dashboard time range.

6be0s85Mk.6: Cumulative Grafana alert evaluation results with state alerting, as exported by grafana_alerting_result_total. Despite the panel title, this counter is not the current number of firing alerts and can reset on restart. No data may mean this legacy alerting metric is not exported.
6be0s85Mk.8: Number of dashboards reported by the selected Grafana instances. Summing multiple replicas can count the same shared dashboard more than once.
6be0s85Mk.10: Grafana build information, including the version labels exported by each selected instance. The metric value is an information marker, not a health score.
6be0s85Mk.2: HTTP requests handled by Grafana per second, grouped by response status code, using the most recent two samples within one minute. 4xx usually indicates client/authentication issues; 5xx indicates server failures.
6be0s85Mk.4: Grafana HTTP request latency in seconds: median (p50), p99 and mean across selected instances, calculated from recent histogram samples. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency.

vkQ0UHxik.2: DNS requests per second over five minutes, grouped by transport protocol (UDP or TCP). The title refers to total traffic rate, not a cumulative request count.
vkQ0UHxik.4: DNS requests per second over five minutes, grouped by question type, such as A for IPv4 addresses and AAAA for IPv6 addresses.
vkQ0UHxik.6: DNS requests per second over five minutes, grouped by the DNS zone handled by CoreDNS. This helps identify which configured zones generate traffic.
vkQ0UHxik.8: DNS requests per second over five minutes, comparing requests with the DNSSEC OK (DO) bit against all requests. The DO bit asks for DNSSEC records; it does not by itself prove successful validation.
vkQ0UHxik.10: UDP DNS request sizes in bytes, showing p50, p90 and p99 over five minutes. A percentile is the size at or below which that percentage of observed requests falls. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero size.
vkQ0UHxik.12: TCP DNS request sizes in bytes, showing p50, p90 and p99 over five minutes. Compare with UDP traffic when investigating larger DNS messages. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero size.
vkQ0UHxik.14: DNS responses per second over five minutes, grouped by response code. NOERROR means a successful DNS response, NXDOMAIN means the name does not exist, and SERVFAIL indicates a resolution failure.
vkQ0UHxik.32: DNS request processing duration in seconds, showing p50, p90 and p99 over five minutes. Higher values mean slower resolution; p99 highlights the slowest tail of observed requests. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency.
vkQ0UHxik.18: UDP DNS response sizes in bytes, showing p50, p90 and p99 over five minutes. Large responses can increase the risk of truncation or transport fallback. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero size.
vkQ0UHxik.20: TCP DNS response sizes in bytes, showing p50, p90 and p99 over five minutes. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero size.
vkQ0UHxik.22: Current number of cached DNS entries by cache type, including successful and denial responses where exported. This is an entry count, not the amount of memory occupied by the cache.
vkQ0UHxik.24: Cache hits and misses per second over five minutes, grouped by cache type. These are event rates, not a hit percentage. More misses can increase upstream DNS work. No data means that no matching metric is being exported or scraped; it does not prove a zero value.

alertmanager-overview.2: Current alerts stored by each Alertmanager instance, summed across alert states. These are alert records, not the number of notifications sent or distinct incidents across replicas.
alertmanager-overview.3: Incoming alerts and invalid alerts per second, grouped by Alertmanager instance. Invalid alerts could not be accepted; repeated updates to the same alert contribute to receive traffic. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency.
alertmanager-overview.5: Notification attempts and failed notifications per second for the selected integration. The total includes failed attempts; it is not a success-only count. Failures mean Alertmanager could not deliver through the receiver. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. No data can mean that this integration has not sent notifications or is not configured.
alertmanager-overview.6: Notification delivery duration in seconds for the selected integration: median (p50), p99 and mean. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency. This measures Alertmanager delivery work, not how quickly a person reads the notification.

3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.1: Number of kubelets with a currently available node-name metric in the selected cluster. This panel does not apply the instance filter and is not a direct check of Kubernetes Node Ready status.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.2: Current number of pods reported as running by the selected kubelets. This is a pod count, not the number of ready containers.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.3: Current number of containers in the running state on selected kubelets. A running container may still fail its readiness check.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.4: Volumes currently recorded in kubelet volume managers' actual state, summed across selected instances. Compare with desired volume count when investigating mounts that have not converged.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.5: Volumes kubelet volume managers expect to manage, summed across selected instances. Temporary differences from actual count can occur while pods and volumes are being created or removed.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.6: The inherited query applies a per-second rate to kubelet_node_config_error. That metric is a configuration-error state gauge, so this result is not a reliable error count or current error state. No data means that no matching metric is being exported or scraped; it does not prove a zero value.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.7: Container runtime operations per second, separated by kubelet instance and operation type, such as listing, creating or stopping containers. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.8: Failed container runtime operations per second, separated by instance and operation type. Compare with operation rate to distinguish increased traffic from a higher failure fraction. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.9: 99th-percentile container runtime operation duration in seconds, separated by instance and operation type. Approximately 99% of observed operations complete within this time. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.10: Pod-start observations and pod-worker operations per second, grouped by instance. The worker series includes pod reconciliation work and is not simply the count of newly created pods. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.11: 99th-percentile pod-start and pod-worker durations in seconds, grouped by instance. Pod start and reconciliation measure different parts of kubelet work. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.12: Volume storage operations per second, grouped by instance, operation name and volume plugin. Activity is expected when volumes are mounted, attached or removed. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.13: Failed storage operations per second, grouped by instance, operation name and volume plugin. Compare with storage operation rate and pod volume events. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.14: 99th-percentile storage operation duration in seconds, grouped by instance, operation name and volume plugin. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.15: Cgroup manager operations per second, grouped by instance and operation type. Cgroups are Linux resource-control groups used to manage containers. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.16: 99th-percentile cgroup manager operation duration in seconds, grouped by instance and operation type. Higher values indicate slower container resource-control work. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.17: Pod Lifecycle Event Generator (PLEG) relists per second by instance. Relisting checks the container runtime for pod state changes. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.18: 99th-percentile interval between Pod Lifecycle Event Generator (PLEG) relists, in seconds, by instance. Longer intervals mean pod runtime state is checked less frequently. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.19: 99th-percentile duration of Pod Lifecycle Event Generator (PLEG) relists in seconds, by instance. Longer relists indicate slower inspection of container runtime state. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.20: Outgoing REST client requests per second from the selected kubelet scrape endpoints, grouped by HTTP status class: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error and 5xx server error. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. In K3s, shared process metrics can include client activity from other components.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.21: 99th-percentile outgoing REST client request duration in seconds, grouped by instance and HTTP method. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency. In K3s, shared process metrics can include client activity from other components.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.22: Resident memory of the process exposed by each kubelet metrics endpoint, in bytes. In K3s this can represent the shared K3s process rather than memory attributable only to kubelet.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.23: CPU time used per second by the process exposed by each kubelet endpoint, expressed in CPU cores: 1 means one full core. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. In K3s this can include other components running in the same process.
3138fa155d5915769fbded898ac09fd9.24: Current number of Go goroutines in the process exposed by each kubelet endpoint. Goroutines are lightweight concurrent tasks, not operating-system threads. In K3s the count can include other components in the same process.

919b92a8e8041bd567af9edab12c840c.1: Used and available filesystem space for the selected persistent volume claim, in bytes. Used space is capacity minus available space; duplicate node reports are reduced before display. This reflects the reported filesystem, which may be larger than the claim for local-path volumes. No data means that no matching metric is being exported or scraped; it does not prove a zero value.
919b92a8e8041bd567af9edab12c840c.2: Percentage of reported filesystem capacity that is unavailable for the selected persistent volume claim: (capacity - available) / capacity. Values approaching 100% indicate little remaining space. Local-path claims may report their shared underlying filesystem. No data means that no matching metric is being exported or scraped; it does not prove a zero value.
919b92a8e8041bd567af9edab12c840c.3: Used and remaining filesystem inodes for the selected persistent volume claim. An inode is a filesystem entry needed for a file or directory; inodes can run out even when free bytes remain. No data means that no matching metric is being exported or scraped; it does not prove a zero value.
919b92a8e8041bd567af9edab12c840c.4: Percentage of filesystem inodes used by the selected persistent volume claim. Values approaching 100% mean few new files can be created even if space remains. Some volume drivers or filesystems do not export inode statistics.

09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.2: Share of API read and write requests meeting the installed success and latency service-level criteria over the recording rule's 30-day window. The dashboard compares this with its 99% target; it is not simply the share of HTTP 2xx responses. With shorter metric retention, the available history may be shorter than 30 days.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.3: Remaining fraction of the error budget for the dashboard's 99% availability target, based on the 30-day availability recording rule. 100% means the full budget remains, 0% means it is exhausted, and a negative value means the target was missed. The window is limited by available retained history.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.4: Share of API read requests (GET and LIST) meeting the installed success and latency criteria over the recording rule's 30-day window. This is a service-level indicator, not just HTTP success rate; available retained history may cover less than 30 days.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.5: API read requests (GET and LIST) per second, grouped by HTTP response code and averaged over five minutes. Compare error responses with total traffic when investigating API availability.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.6: Fraction of API read requests returning HTTP 5xx, grouped by resource and calculated from five-minute rates. A missing result can mean there were no requests or no matching error series, rather than a confirmed zero.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.7: API read latency in seconds from the installed histogram-quantile recording rule, grouped by its resource and quantile labels. Higher values mean slower GET/LIST operations. The rule defines the calculation window; idle resources may have no percentile value.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.8: Share of API write requests (POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE) meeting the installed success and latency criteria over the recording rule's 30-day window. Available retained history may cover less than 30 days.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.9: API write requests (POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE) per second, grouped by HTTP response code and averaged over five minutes.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.10: Fraction of API write requests returning HTTP 5xx, grouped by resource and calculated from five-minute rates. A missing result can mean there were no requests or no matching error series, rather than a confirmed zero.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.11: API write latency in seconds from the installed histogram-quantile recording rule, grouped by its resource and quantile labels. Higher values mean slower write operations. The rule defines the calculation window; idle resources may have no percentile value.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.12: Items added to API server work queues per second, grouped by instance and queue name. A rise indicates more background work arriving, not necessarily a backlog. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.13: The inherited query applies a per-second rate to workqueue_depth, which is a gauge of currently queued items. This is not the actual queue depth and should not be interpreted as the number of waiting tasks. No data means that no matching metric is being exported or scraped; it does not prove a zero value.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.14: 99th-percentile time that items wait in API server work queues before processing, in seconds, grouped by instance and queue name. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. Gaps can occur when no observations were recorded in the calculation interval; they do not mean zero latency.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.15: Resident memory in bytes of the process exposed by each API server endpoint. K3s can share this process with other control-plane components, so this is not necessarily API-server-only memory.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.16: CPU time used per second by each process exposed through the API server endpoint, expressed in CPU cores: 1 means one full core. Rates use Grafana's automatic rate interval, which adapts to the displayed time range and scrape frequency. In K3s this can include other components in the same process.
09ec8aa1e996d6ffcd6817bbaff4db1b.17: Current number of Go goroutines in the process exposed by each API server endpoint. Goroutines are lightweight concurrent tasks. In K3s this can include other control-plane components sharing the process.
